processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Raw materials of high purity (>99.9 %) melted in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere; nominal composition Fe-35Mn-15Al-5Cu (at.%).
Ingots homogenized at 1200 °C for 24 h before hot rolling.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates of 4 mm thickness, then cut into 10×5×2 mm³ samples by electrical discharge machining.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated sample aged at 525 °C for 6 h, followed by water quenching. This is the terminal aging step defining the sample state.

structures.overall_structure: Aged 15Al condition: the α (BCC) matrix is largely transformed to β-Mn. The 525 °C/6 h SE-SEM micrograph shows a mostly uniform (essentially transformed) β-Mn matrix crossed by a curved boundary with a green β-Mn arrow; residual untransformed α persists at the shorter 3 h/525 °C step, and abundant fine new precipitates develop only at longer times (10 h).

phases_present.morphology: short rod-shaped at nucleation, developing into a near-uniform transformed matrix; green-labelled in SE/phase maps
residual untransformed α regions largely consumed by β-Mn at 525 °C; at the intermediate 525 °C/3 h step residual α was still imaged (labelled 'Untransformed α')

precipitates.distribution: at the interfaces between β-Mn (documented for the peak-hardness 15Al condition, not specifically for 525 °C/6 h)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and averaged

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester; load 9.8 N; dwell 15 s; each sample measured 5 times and averaged
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify the aging-hardening response (hardness) of the 15Al alloy after aging
characterization_methods.key_findings: 15Al aged at 525 °C for 6 h gives 916.8 ± 8.7 HV

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: electrolytically polished samples (10 % perchloric acid + 90 % ethanol); 50 μm main-field scale bars with 10 μm insets
characterization_methods.purpose: Image second-phase precipitation (α-Mn and β-Mn) in the aged 15Al alloy
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fig. 7 includes a 525 °C/6 h panel showing a mostly uniform (largely β-Mn) matrix crossed by a curved boundary with a green β-Mn label.

unmapped_findings: The 85.8 % β-Mn fraction measured by EBSD for the 15Al alloy (b0040, Fig. 4) corresponds to aging at 525 °C for 3 h, NOT the 6 h condition of this sample; for 525 °C/6 h only the SE-SEM Fig. 7 panel (mostly uniform β-Mn matrix, curved boundary, green β-Mn label) is available.
The fracture toughness values (KIC = 8.6 MPa·m^1/2 for 15Al) were measured on the PEAK-hardness samples (HV = 965.6 for 15Al, i.e. 600 °C/6 h), not on the 525 °C/6 h sample (b0021, b0061).

The TEM/HRTEM interface characterization of fine FCC Cu-rich particles with FCC twins at β-Mn interfaces (Figs. 11, 12; b0057, b0058) was performed on the 15Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 6 h and the 17Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 6 h — not on the 525 °C/6 h sample.

The intrinsic β-Mn nanoindentation hardness (12.1 ± 0.3 GPa for 15Al) and the average nanoindentation hardness (11.7 ± 0.4 GPa) were measured on the hardest 15Al sample (600 °C/6 h), not on the 525 °C/6 h sample (b0060, figure_013).
The ultra-high specific hardness of 141 HV·cm³/g was reported for the peak-hardness Fe-35.2Mn-15Al-5.2Cu (15Al) state (HV = 965.6, i.e. 600 °C/6 h), not for the 525 °C/6 h condition (b0008, b0077).
The XRD phase identification (α/D0₃ + α-Mn + β-Mn) shown in Fig. 10 was performed on the 15Al alloy aged at 550 °C for 1 h, not on the 525 °C/6 h sample (b0053, figure_010).
The β-Mn micro-area composition (Mn 36.8 at.%, Al 14.3 at.%, Cu 2.8 at.% for 15Al) was measured on the hardest 15Al sample by SEM-EDS (Fig. 14, b0060).

For the 15Al alloy, the hardness at 525 °C increased only slightly after 1 h (379.8 ± 19.1 HV) and then rose sharply by 6 h (916.8 ± 8.7 HV) and 10 h (915.7 ± 9.5 HV), i.e. low-temperature aging requires ~6 h to reach the >900 HV plateau (b0028, b0037).
The optimal aging temperature range for achieving ultra-high hardness in the 15Al alloy is reported mainly as 525 °C–600 °C (b0038).
